structures.questionTemplate: Two similar figures have corresponding side lengths of $${scope.l1}\text{ cm}$ and $${scope.l2}\text{ cm}$. If the area of the first figure is $${scope.A1}\text{ cm}^2$, find the unknown area $A_2$.
steps: State the area ratio formula for similar figures: $$\frac{A_2}{A_1} = \left(\frac{l_2}{l_1}\right)^2$$

Substitute the given values into the formula: $$\frac{A_2}{${scope.A1}} = \left(\frac{${scope.l2}}{${scope.l1}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{${scope.red_l2}}{${scope.red_l1}}\right)^2 = \frac{${scope.a_sq}}{${scope.b_sq}}$$
Solve for $A_2$: $$A_2 = ${scope.A1} \times \frac{${scope.a_sq}}{${scope.b_sq}} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}^2$$

structures.questionTemplate: Two similar solids have heights of $${scope.h1}\text{ cm}$ and $${scope.h2}\text{ cm}$ respectively. If the volume of the first solid is $${scope.V1}\text{ cm}^3$, find the volume of the second solid $V_2$.
steps: State the volume ratio formula for similar solids: $$\frac{V_2}{V_1} = \left(\frac{h_2}{h_1}\right)^3$$

Substitute the given values into the formula: $$\frac{V_2}{${scope.V1}} = \left(\frac{${scope.h2}}{${scope.h1}}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{${scope.red_h2}}{${scope.red_h1}}\right)^3 = \frac{${scope.a3}}{${scope.b3}}$$
Solve for $V_2$: $$V_2 = ${scope.V1} \times \frac{${scope.a3}}{${scope.b3}} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}^3$$

structures.questionTemplate: Two similar figures have areas of $${scope.A1}\text{ cm}^2$ and $${scope.A2}\text{ cm}^2$. If a side length of the first figure is $${scope.l1}\text{ cm}$, find the corresponding side length $x$ of the second figure.
steps: State the linear length ratio formula derived from area ratio: $$\frac{x}{l_1} = \sqrt{\frac{A_2}{A_1}}$$
Substitute the given values into the formula: $$\frac{x}{${scope.l1}} = \sqrt{\frac{${scope.A2}}{${scope.A1}}} = \frac{${scope.a}}{${scope.b}}$$
Solve for $x$: $$x = ${scope.l1} \times \frac{${scope.a}}{${scope.b}} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}$$

structures.questionTemplate: In $\Delta ABC$, $DE \parallel BC$ such that $D$ lies on $AB$ and $E$ lies on $AC$. Given $AD = ${scope.ad}\text{ cm}$, $BD = ${scope.bd}\text{ cm}$, and the area of $\Delta ADE$ is $${scope.areaADE}\text{ cm}^2$, find the area of $\Delta ABC$.
steps: Calculate total length $AB$: $$AB = AD + BD = ${scope.ad} + ${scope.bd} = ${scope.ab}\text{ cm}$$
State the area ratio formula for similar triangles $\Delta ABC \sim \Delta ADE$: $$\frac{\text{Area}(\Delta ABC)}{\text{Area}(\Delta ADE)} = \left(\frac{AB}{AD}\right)^2$$

Substitute the given side lengths into the formula: $$\frac{\text{Area}(\Delta ABC)}{${scope.areaADE}} = \left(\frac{${scope.ab}}{${scope.ad}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{${scope.num}}{${scope.den}}\right)^2 = \frac{${scope.num_sq}}{${scope.den_sq}}$$
Solve for $\text{Area}(\Delta ABC)$: $$\text{Area}(\Delta ABC) = ${scope.areaADE} \times \frac{${scope.num_sq}}{${scope.den_sq}} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}^2$$

structures.questionTemplate: The perimeters of two similar pentagons are $${scope.p1}\text{ cm}$ and $${scope.p2}\text{ cm}$ respectively. Find the ratio of their areas in simplest form $a : b$.
steps: State the area ratio formula based on perimeter ratio: $$\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)^2$$

Substitute values and simplify the fraction: $$\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \left(\frac{${scope.p1}}{${scope.p2}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{${scope.n1}}{${scope.n2}}\right)^2 = \frac{${scope.n1_sq}}{${scope.n2_sq}}$$
Convert the simplified fraction into a ratio: $$\text{Ratio of areas } A_1 : A_2 = ${scope.n1_sq} : ${scope.n2_sq}$$

structures.questionTemplate: The ratio of the areas of corresponding faces of two similar cubes is $${scope.areaB} : ${scope.areaA}$. If the volume of the smaller cube is $${scope.volB}\text{ cm}^3$, find the volume of the larger cube.
steps: Find the linear side ratio from the area ratio: $$\frac{l_2}{l_1} = \sqrt{\frac{A_2}{A_1}} = \sqrt{\frac{${scope.areaA}}{${scope.areaB}}} = \frac{${scope.a}}{${scope.b}}$$
State the volume ratio formula: $$\frac{V_2}{V_1} = \left(\frac{l_2}{l_1}\right)^3$$
Substitute the linear scale factor into the volume ratio formula: $$\frac{V_2}{${scope.volB}} = \left(\frac{${scope.a}}{${scope.b}}\right)^3 = \frac{${scope.a3}}{${scope.b3}}$$
Solve for the volume of the larger cube $V_2$: $$V_2 = ${scope.volB} \times \frac{${scope.a3}}{${scope.b3}} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}^3$$

structures.questionTemplate: A solid cone of total height $${scope.H}\text{ cm}$ has a total volume of $${scope.vTotal}\text{ cm}^3$. A smaller cone of height $${scope.h1}\text{ cm}$ is sliced off parallel to the base. Find the volume of the remaining frustum.
steps: State the height ratio of the top small cone to the full cone: $$\frac{h_{\text{top}}}{H} = \frac{${scope.h1}}{${scope.H}} = \frac{${scope.small_den}}{${scope.big_num}}$$

Calculate the volume of the sliced top cone $V_{\text{top}}$: $$\frac{V_{\text{top}}}{V_{\text{total}}} = \left(\frac{h_{\text{top}}}{H}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{${scope.small_den}}{${scope.big_num}}\right)^3 = \frac{${scope.small_cubed}}{${scope.big_cubed}}$$
Find $V_{\text{top}}$: $$V_{\text{top}} = ${scope.vTotal} \times \frac{${scope.small_cubed}}{${scope.big_cubed}} = ${scope.vTop}\text{ cm}^3$$
Subtract $V_{\text{top}}$ from total volume to get the volume of the frustum: $$V_{\text{frustum}} = V_{\text{total}} - V_{\text{top}} = ${scope.vTotal} - ${scope.vTop} = ${scope.ans}\text{ cm}^3$$
